newsitem.title: USA: Michigan judge hears Dow implant arguments.
newsitem.headline: Michigan judge hears Dow implant arguments.

text.p: A federal judge in Michigan on Monday took under advisement arguments on whether a two-month-old Louisiana state breast implant class action trial can proceed against Dow Chemical Co.
U.S. District Court Judge Denise Page Hood had not made a decision by late Monday afternoon when she would issue her ruling following an emergency hearing requested by plaintiff lawyers.

The closely watched case, one of the first class action breast implant lawsuits to go to trial against Dow Chemical, has been in limbo since an appeals court ruling that thousands of implant lawsuits around the country should be consolidated in Michigan federal court.

That ruling upheld a request from Dow Corning Corp that cases against it and its owners, Dow Chemical and Corning Inc, be shifted into one court to facilitate Dow Corning's bankrupcty court reorganization plan.
Attorneys representing about 1,700 women suing Dow Chemical want Hood to grant a "mandatory abstention" from the ruling by the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals in Cincinnati on May 8.
Plaintiff lawyer Dawn Barrios accused Dow Chemical of delaying the Louisiana case as long as possible and continuing a pattern of "shopping" for friendly judges in various courts.
"They're seeking another judge to take this case out of the hands of 12 jurors," she said.
But attorneys for Dow Corning and Dow Chemical said plaintiffs attorneys are to blame for pushing ahead with the trial in March despite the unresolved appeals court issue.
"Your honor, this is a self-inflicted wound," said Dow Corning attorney Barbara Houser.

Dow Corning of Midland, Mich., once the world's largest maker of silicone gel breast implants, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy court protection two years ago. The filing put on hold thousands of lawsuits from women who allege the implants have caused numerous health problems, including lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. Dow Corning denies the claims.

Although Midland-based Dow Chemical did not make the implants, plaintiffs have sued the company because it did some silicone testing. Dow Chemical claims the testing was not related to breast implants.
